title: Personal information · Signs, symbols and purpose
learn: A sign gives a short message. EXIT shows a way out; NO ENTRY means do not go in. An arrow gives a direction. A notice with a date and time often tells you about an event. Look at words and layout together, then decide what to do.
worked_example:
Question: Why does the notice show an event heading, date and time?
Model answer: To help readers attend the session.
Why: The layout makes the event arrangements easy to find.
guided_practice: Use the first checked task to practise the rule or strategy. Read its explanation, correct an error and explain why the answer fits. For the productive tasks, compare your response with the example and rubric before revising.

Park Learning Centre
Information session
Monday 25 January 2027 at 13:30
Room 5
Bring your reference card.
Contact: Amina
Reference: BE-1401

SIGNS
EXIT → : way out to the right
NO ENTRY: do not go in
PULL: pull the door towards you

PRACTICE GLOSSARY (alphabetical)
available — free or ready to be used
record — information kept about a person or event
session — a period of time used for a particular activity
support — help given to someone

title: Personal information · Capitals and full stops
learn: Start a sentence with a capital and finish a statement with a full stop. Write I as a capital even in the middle of a sentence. Names also need capitals. Read your work aloud and check where each complete idea ends.
worked_example:
Question: Choose the correctly punctuated statement.
